name: Ultranationalism
summary: An extreme form of nationalism that asserts the supremacy of one nation over others and subordinates the individual to the nation-state. Typical accounts describe a mythic story of national decline and rebirth, hostility to foreigners and minorities, militarism and expansion, authoritarian leadership and rejection of liberal democracy and class-based socialism.
scope: The interwar-style core of ultranationalism as described by Roger Griffin and Janusz Bugajski, drawing on Fascist Italy (The Doctrine of Fascism), Maurras's integral nationalism and Japanese kokutai ultranationalism. It excludes ordinary patriotic or civic nationalism and contemporary strands such as Hindutva or Russian imperialism, which are not profiled here. Because the strands differ on race, religion and economics, many answers on those topics are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Japanese ultranationalism: divine emperor, family-state, nation before self, mobilization, hakko ichiu.

universal-healthcare.rationale: State care of the national stock fits a strong, nation-serving state, but no source addresses healthcare; inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Indifferent in the sources; wages were set by the state or syndicates rather than by a minimum-wage doctrine.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The State subordinates economic activity to national ends, so markets do not decide; inferred from the Doctrine's state primacy.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherent regimes were split between nationalizing strategic industry and keeping private firms under state direction.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: No documented stance; adherents focus on national unity of classes rather than redistribution.

unions-good.rationale: Independent unions are dissolved into state-controlled syndicates because groups outside the State are rejected.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property is held subject to the State's and nation's needs; inferred from state primacy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The State directs economic life in the national interest; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare for the national community is not opposed in principle; inferred rejection of a cut-welfare libertarian line.

worker-ownership.rationale: Class unity under the State rather than worker control; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Authoritarian ultranationalist states rely on security surveillance against enemies of the nation.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian, order-minded and degeneracy-fearing outlook.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Adherents resist limits on speech against designated enemies; inferred, no direct statement.

strong-leader.rationale: Griffin-style and Bugajski accounts stress a charismatic leader, and the Doctrine accepts the will of One.

state-harmful.rationale: Everything is in the State; nothing human or spiritual has value outside it.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from the state monopoly on force; some strands arm loyal citizens.

empower-police-military.rationale: Militarism is central, and Japanese ultranationalism sought a mobilized military nation.

decide-locally.rationale: Unity and centralized national will dominate; the kokutai and the State are unitary.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on order and punishment of enemies.

traditional-family.rationale: The Japanese family-state pictured the nation as one family; Fascism sees the family as a component of the State.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from traditionalism and natalism.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from natalist concern for the nation's body.

more-religion-public.rationale: Fascism is called a religious conception, Maurras wanted a Church role, and Shinto was fused with the state.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Race and nation hierarchies are central; redress for minorities runs against the supremacist outlook.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from organic, traditionalist view of society.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mythic national culture is central; Maurras excluded 'Anti-France' elements to protect it.

gradual-change.rationale: Palingenetic rebirth calls for radical renewal, though tradition is revered.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Xenophobia is described as foundational and foreigners were seen as unassimilable.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Disdain of other nations and assertion of national supremacy reject supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: Nation-first economics favours autarky and protection; inferred from sources' state-directed economy.

nation-first.rationale: Defined by asserting national hegemony and interests over other nations.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Force is used for national interest, not human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Contradicts xenophobia and exclusion of foreigners.

limit-growth.rationale: Growth and power serve the nation; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; some strands frame climate policy as capitulation to foreign interests.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The BUF stressed technological progress; otherwise inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from power and self-sufficiency aims.

revolution-justified.rationale: Radical national rebirth and violent movements, though aimed against liberal or communist order.

experts-over-public.rationale: Adherents rely on the leader's will rather than either experts or the public.

central-planning.rationale: The State directs the economy but no source commits to a planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Class and worker ownership are not goals; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family and tradition are valued; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economics favours protection of national industry.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The State organizes and directs national activity.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Maurras favoured organic small units but it is not a general ultranationalist demand.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Rejection of socialism and class abolition.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The State controls economic life; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Doctrine's syndicates and unity of classes in the State; Maurras favoured organic bodies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Bugajski links extreme forms to a movement-style party; Maurras's monarchist strand differs.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Maurras's monarchism and the divine emperor of Japan, though fascist strands were republican.

democracy-best.rationale: Opposes liberal democracy; the Doctrine rejects rule by majority.

direct-votes.rationale: Rejects majority rule and democratic governance.

workers-councils.rationale: Class-based power rejected in favour of the unified State.

right-to-secede.rationale: Ultranationalists treat the nation as a living organism whose unity and territory must be defended, which implies denying any right to secede, though the sources do not discuss secession.

natural-rulers.rationale: Griffin describes hierarchy of superior and degenerate; the Doctrine accepts rule by a few or One.

political-violence-never.rationale: Violence is linked with the movements, and life is conceived as struggle.

war-builds-character.rationale: Militarism is central to ultranationalism and the Doctrine conceives of life as struggle; Japan sought a Sparta-like military nation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Unity of religion and government in Japan and Maurras's role for the Church.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Religion supports the state but laws come from the State's will.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism makes the State the authority that governs and gives laws their form, which implies keeping force public; privatising it is not discussed.

military-superiority.rationale: Supremacy and hegemony over other nations are the definition.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Many strands are ethnic, though Mussolini denied race as the nation's basis.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Socialism is rejected for confining history to class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy is accepted; qualitative not quantitative view of the nation.

colonial-reparations.rationale: National pride and expansionism reject guilt for imperial acts.

civilizational-union.rationale: Japan's Co-Prosperity Sphere and Russian imperial strands are union under a dominant nation; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The nation is put before the self.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Individuals matter only as they coincide with the State; put nation before self.

limit-population.rationale: Expansion and national strength imply natalism; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from emphasis on national power and technology.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Adherents revere inherited institutions but sometimes champion technology.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Rule by will of the leader and State; inferred.

restore-past-order.rationale: Myths of past greatness and rebirth of a decayed nation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Fascism claims to be a doctrine, a religious conception, not pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Movements have used violence and extra-parliamentary action; liberal parliaments are rejected.

means-match-ends.rationale: Struggle and force are accepted as means; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism praises work by which man conquers nature, and ultranationalism seeks national power, which implies rejecting a return to foraging; the idea is not discussed.

production-for-use.rationale: Production serves the nation, not need as such; inferred.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism says no class can exist outside the State and opposes socialism for ignoring the unity of classes within the State, which excludes the rule of one class over others.

collective-farming.rationale: Not documented; inferred from rejection of socialism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Rejects Marxist theory; war is a product of national struggle.

taxation-theft.rationale: Individual claims against the State are rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: Mussolini's Doctrine declares that everything is in the State and nothing human or spiritual has value outside it; the State is the discipline of the whole person, not a mechanism limiting itself to individual liberties.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The Doctrine sets itself against individualism, accepting the individual only in so far as he coincides with the State, and calls the State the creator of right.

conscription.rationale: Militarism and mobilization of the whole population.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit presupposes individual primacy over the nation.

state-as-business.rationale: The Doctrine's State is an ethical and spiritual reality outside which nothing has value, which implies rejecting the image of citizens as customers free to leave, though it does not address that model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom is defined as service to the State, not material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Adherents split; only some strands target media and academia.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Nazi strand yes; Mussolini and Maurras do not base nation on race.

organic-representation.rationale: Maurras favoured organic bodies such as family, locality; the Doctrine's syndicates.

total-state.rationale: Everything is in the State; nothing outside it.

national-rebirth.rationale: Griffin says ultranationalism draws legitimacy from mythicised narratives of past greatness and divides societies into the degenerate and those with great destinies; Fascist Italy and Nazi Germany built on it with plans for national renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Hegemony, expansion of the State, hakko ichiu.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalty to leader and State not feudal oaths; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Modern mass-mobilizing movements, not feudal; inferred.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Some strands disparage 'foreign' science; not a defining view.

universal-morality.rationale: Particular national destinies; moral value rests in the State.

single-common-good.rationale: National unity above classes and interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Adherents split; some strands are hostile, Israeli settler movements are ultranationalist.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Rejects class-based and democratic workplace control.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education is directed by the State; inferred.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Not documented; state-driven spending is acceptable.

economic-freedom.rationale: Freedom is subordinate to the State.

rule-by-example.rationale: Rule relies on force and the leader's will.

national-self-determination.rationale: The ideology asserts hegemony over other nations.

force-without-un.rationale: Disdain for other nations and international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Fascism is called a religious conception, valuing will and myth.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Exclusion of foreigners from the national community.

class-collaboration.rationale: Unity of classes in the State; solidarity over class struggle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Reverence for national heritage and myth.

dominated-front.rationale: Russian and Japanese strands framed fronts against the West; inferred.

workers-nation.rationale: Workers organized within the nation, not as international class.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation is associated with ultranationalism per the source.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Doctrine rejects socialism for confining history to class struggle and holds that classes are unified in one economic and moral reality in the State, the opposite of the Marxist view.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Exclusion or forced assimilation of foreigners.

elite-replacement.rationale: Modern conspiracy strand only; not defining.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Patriarchal order is affirmed as natural.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Movements attack the liberal political class.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Griffin notes eugenics used to rationalize degeneracy.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Defends the forces serving the nation.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Doctrine says the Fascist State cannot confine itself to the functions of order and supervision as Liberalism desired, but takes over all forms of moral and intellectual life.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Orban's cited condemnation; inferred for racial strands.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religion tied to nation in some strands.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Church or Shinto role in education.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Authority rests on the State and leader.

population-transfer.rationale: Hostility towards minorities; genocide and expulsions in Ustase and other cases.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The Doctrine conceives of life as a struggle, and ultranationalist accounts stress domination among nations.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Movements oppose such bans in opposition; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not a republican or liberal view.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and adherents have no shared position on housing tenure.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Class conflict is suppressed in the State.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from natalist and expansionist outlook that treats population as strength.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Minorities seen as hostile and unassimilable.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Rule by a few or One, not chance.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The State may override individual protection.

party-commands-army.rationale: Split: Nazi oath to leader versus independent Japanese army.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Violence against enemies of the nation is accepted and life is conceived as struggle.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from the described xenophobia and view of foreigners as unassimilable, which imply keeping outsiders from full membership for a long time; no source gives residence periods.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Ultranationalist regimes made office a mark of rank and national service, not ordinary wages; nothing in the sources addresses pay, so this is inferred.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Mussolini's doctrine demands the individual's subordination to the party and state, and fascist parties enforced strict obedience to decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Ultranationalism asserts the supremacy and full sovereignty of the nation and rejects subordination to supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Ultranationalist doctrines favour a strong authoritarian leader or emperor commanding the military and choosing ministers, as in the Duce and kokutai models.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Integral nationalists such as Maurras and kokutai writers favoured hierarchical, state-aligned religion over congregational control; inferred, as strands differ on religion.

clerical-rule.rationale: Ultranationalism places the nation-state, not clergy, at the top, though it often allies with established religion; inferred from that.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Ultranationalism demands loyalty to the nation in war and treats defeatism as treason, rejecting class-over-nation internationalism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Ultranationalist states censored art and culture to serve national renewal and moral discipline, though the justification is national more than strictly moral.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Ultranationalist regimes keep the leader in power without term limits and reject liberal constitutional checks.

recall-officials.rationale: Voter recall conflicts with authoritarian leadership and the rejection of liberal democracy that typical accounts describe.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Ultranationalists seek national strength and expansion, which usually means military power abroad rather than withdrawal; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism wants the state to organise the nation through corporations and property, with no case for banning rent; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism glorifies war and the militia but keeps a disciplined state army; replacing it with an armed citizenry is not supported; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nationalist myths of national rebirth often prize the peasantry and the rural soil over cities; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Irredentism and the unification of co-nationals in one state are central to ultranationalist accounts.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Maurras and other integral nationalists distrusted liberal intellectuals, though ultranationalists also prize their own elites; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Ultranationalism asserts the supremacy of one nation over others, which contradicts any claim that cultures are equal.

death-penalty.rationale: Authoritarian, order-focused nationalism favours harsh state punishment, but no source addresses capital punishment directly; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Authoritarian nationalism subordinates schooling to national and traditional values, so gender equality education is not favoured; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Strands differ, with some tied to the church and others secular; no source addresses creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Authoritarian nationalist states favour moral discipline and censorship of public culture; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Integral nationalism defines the nation by ancestry and blood, so citizenship passes by descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Ultranationalism is hostile to minorities and demands one national culture and language; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Ultranationalists subordinate religious minorities to the nation and the state, so exemptions are not favoured; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism subordinates the individual to the state and rejects individualism, so encouraging eccentricity is opposed; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The sources do not address foreign debt; hostility to foreign creditors and state primacy pull against any one answer.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Ultranationalism treats national independence and the nation-state as ends in themselves rather than depending on economic transformation; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Ultranationalism rejects liberal democracy and parliamentary procedure in favour of authoritarian leadership, so an elected constituent assembly is opposed.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The individual is subordinated to the nation-state and authoritarian rule is accepted; the growth rationale itself is inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Asserting the supremacy of one nation and hostility to foreigners rule out a duty of aid owed to the world poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Militarism and national self-reliance suggest an independent deterrent; inferred, as the sources predate nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Ultranationalism favours authoritarian leadership, not popular election of the head of state; the Japanese kokutai model rests on a sacred emperor. Inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A state that dominates the economy for national ends would not give monetary policy to an independent body; inferred.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Expansion and mythic national rebirth make ceding claimed national land unacceptable.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Fascist-style ultranationalism subordinates private interests to the nation, implying property serves national ends; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Ultranationalists reject class-based socialism, but the sources say nothing on how they classify the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk is outside the ideology's concerns, so adherents are indifferent; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Automatic mutual-defence duties sit badly with national supremacy and sovereignty; alliances are treated as instruments of national interest. Inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Expansion and annexation are accepted aims of ultranationalism, so annexation is not treated as unlawful occupation; inferred from its militarism and expansionism.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism holds the state embraces and shapes every institution, and kokutai ideology bound the shrine religion to the state; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Maurras and kokutai put the monarch above politics, but the fascist leader heads the party and takes sides; strands are split.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: An indivisible nation whose unity is paramount implies that secession may be put down by force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Ultranationalism stresses one unified national order and culture, so a region with its own system is disfavoured; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Kokutai ideology rests on the emperor's divine descent, though other strands such as Italian Fascism did not make rulers sacred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Ultranationalism has no tax doctrine and its strands differ on economics; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Ultranationalism tends to ground the nation in blood, soil and inherited spirit, though it also stresses national education; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism makes the state the source of law and values, with nothing above it, which implies the ruler is not bound.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic for the interwar core; the ideology values national grandeur but does not address it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects power-sharing between estates and parties in favour of unitary authority; inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Fascist Italy and imperial Japan cultivated reverence for the Duce and the emperor as embodiments of the nation, though Maurras did not.

equal-parenting.rationale: Ultranationalism does not address custody law; adherents have no settled position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects class struggle and socialism in favour of national unity.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from protection of property within a class-collaborating nation.

refugee-return.rationale: Hostility to foreigners and minorities, as described by Griffin and Bugajski, implies opposition; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Accounts describe expansion and claims on territory held by the nation’s own people.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed; the national state, not religious law, is the supreme value, so inferred.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not addressed; the family-state tradition of dress is set by national custom, so inferred.

common-currency.rationale: National sovereignty over its own affairs implies a separate currency; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-movements and the Japanese hakko ichiu idea show a drive toward unity of kin peoples under one nation; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Ultranationalism is hostile to minorities and expects one nation in the state.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Nationalists treat minorities as outsiders, so equal rights where they live is not endorsed; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The doctrine places spirit, nation and will above class and economy; inferred from the Doctrine of Fascism.

ban-cartels.rationale: The corporate state directs the economy; inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: The nation-serving state would rescue national firms; inferred.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The state and nation are supreme over legal limits and liberal institutions; inferred.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The traditional family and gender roles of the movement oppose quotas; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Fascist Italy and imperial Japan pursued autarky and closed economic blocs; inferred.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Supranational standards are at odds with national supremacy; inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Subordinating the individual to the nation implies duty over private gain; inferred.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism glorifies action and violence as the path to national rebirth; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Strands differ: Maurras is monarchist and Japan upheld an emperor, but Mussolini’s fascists were republican.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Kokutai no Hongi and the fascist doctrine make the nation's own history and spirit the core of education.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from the expansionist, civilising-empire rhetoric of Mussolini's doctrine and hakko ichiu; sources do not state it as tutelage.

patriotic-education.rationale: Kokutai no Hongi and fascist education mobilise schooling for national loyalty and reverence for national symbols.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from nation-before-individual and hostility to minorities; sources do not address admissions or hiring preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of the state over the economy in the Doctrine of Fascism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Inferred: the Doctrine rejects Marxist materialism and class-war collapse, but does not address capitalist crises directly.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Expansion and the reclaiming of former imperial lands are central: Italian restored-Roman-empire claims and Japanese hakko ichiu.

delink-world-market.rationale: Inferred from fascist autarky and economic nationalism; the sources do not discuss poor countries' policy.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Inferred from the doctrine of class unity within the nation, which denies the rich-country worker's separate interests.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of private owners and individuals to the state.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects liberalism and individual rights against the state.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: irredentist, nation-first ultranationalism treats divisions of a nation imposed by outsiders as illegitimate.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred: the strands favour authoritarian, charismatic or dynastic leadership over electing rulers, though the Italian and Maurrasian models differ.

minority-veto.rationale: The nation-state takes precedence over the individual, so a dissenting minority cannot hold a veto against it.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred: authority and obedience to the leader or emperor are central, so resistance to a ruler is not endorsed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Ultranationalism rejects liberal parliamentary democracy in favour of authoritarian leadership.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The strands do not address animals; adherents are indifferent or split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred: in the absence of doctrine, ordinary acceptance of animal use is the default.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred: class solidarity and duty within the national community are stressed, though as national duty rather than charity.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Individuals owe active service and mobilization to the nation, so withdrawal from public life is rejected.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: ultranationalist movements use mass media and culture to mobilize rather than pacify, and do not frame them as reproducing the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: the strands stress will, force and myth over consent won through liberal institutions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred: adherents are split between rhetoric of exploited nations and hierarchy among nations; the sources do not address it.

native-born-offices.rationale: Exclusion of foreigners from the national community is a core trait, extending to reserving public posts for the native nation.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred: national sovereignty and independence from outside direction are prized, though the statement concerns socialist parties.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred: autarkic national self-sufficiency fits the nation-first outlook.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial expansion and recovery of national lands are standard features of ultranationalism.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the strands put the founding national people first, but the statement concerns pre-colonial peoples over settlers, which they do not address.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascist and ultranationalist doctrine is explicitly anti-liberal and anti-socialist and rejects anti-fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred: adherents condemn communism but embrace the strong state, so reject equivalence with their own order.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The ideology does not address the American Civil War; adherents are split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred: reverence for national history and heroes favours keeping monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred: not addressed; martial manliness is stressed but adherents are split on programmes for men.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Each nation is held to have its own organic form of state, and liberal democracy is rejected as a universal model.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Militarism and the armed forces as guardians of the nation are central, as in Japanese ultranationalism.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: the family-state and national duty frame domestic work as service to the nation, not wage labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from Kokutai no Hongi's family-state, where filial piety models loyalty to the emperor.

office-by-exam.rationale: Inferred: the Doctrine of Fascism favours hierarchy and leader selection, not examinations.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Inferred from state primacy and the nation's supremacy over foreign interests.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the family-state ideal and organic national community.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine of Fascism's rejection of democracy and delegated mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from state primacy and corporatist class unity over private market provision.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Strands differ; the nation outranks the individual but private land often persists.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine of Fascism's open rejection of parliamentary democracy.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from the organic nation and exclusion of foreigners in Maurras's integral nationalism.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Inferred from hostility to foreigners and minorities described by Bugajski.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from Griffin's account of national supremacy, which rejects equality-of-outcome tests.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Inferred from the Doctrine of Fascism's rejection of materialism and comfort.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from militarism and expansion described in the standard accounts.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from national supremacy and hakko ichiu expansion, which justify dominance over neighbours.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates private interests to the state, so adherents would see business money in politics as illegitimate; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Hostility to foreign influence and a nation-first stance imply support for restricting foreign funding; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Fascist doctrine prizes national vigour and numbers, and favours natality over immigration; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Reserving the nation's land for its own people fits the xenophobic strand; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Corporatist states organised labour and provided work in the national interest, but no job guarantee is stated; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: The Doctrine rejects pacifism and democracy and sees struggle and expansion as the nation's vitality.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The Doctrine holds that the state is the source of all value and the individual is subordinate to it.

non-intervention.rationale: Ultranationalists demand sovereignty for their own nation but claim a right to expand over others, so reject a universal ban; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Fascist corporatism organised workers and employers by sector under the state; inferred as sympathetic to industry-wide bodies.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Maurras's integral nationalism blames Jews, Protestants, Freemasons and foreigners as hostile "confederated states"; the strands differ.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Kokutai ideology presents the nation as a family-state, and the family is a pillar of national order.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Authoritarian state primacy and secrecy fit poorly with a right to government records; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Economic nationalism and autarky are typical of the strand; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The Doctrine insists on hierarchical party and state organisation, not informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The Doctrine makes the state sovereign and the supreme authority, with no higher law above the nation.

religious-nation.rationale: Maurras backed the Catholic Church, Fascist Italy was secular-leaning and Japan used state Shinto, so strands split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Supremacy of one's own nation implies other states yielding to it; inferred, as no source addresses tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Subordinating parts to the nation-state points to national pooling over regional retention; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects socialism and class-based common ownership while keeping private property under state direction.

defeat-communism.rationale: Ultranationalism is described as rejecting class-based socialism and Marxism, and fascism treated communism as an enemy.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Corporatist state direction could use private providers, but sources do not address it; adherents are split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Strands tend to treat religion as part of national heritage rather than an illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism denies the doctrine of material progress; inferred as hostile to a progressive reading of capitalism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Traditional gender roles and rejection of class-based analysis; inferred from the interwar sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Family and nation are seen as the units of the nation, so care is left to the family; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism and cultural supremacy are common in the strands described; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Hostility to minorities and subordination to the state makes binding treaties with internal nations unlikely; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Ultranationalism places the nation-state above all and the individual beneath it, opposing decentralised communal property.

majority-settlement.rationale: Assimilation and expansion of the dominant nation into minority areas are described in the sources; settlement policy is inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects both liberal capitalism and socialism in favour of a national corporate order.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Mythic national soil and rebirth narratives imply stronger claims for the historic nation; not directly sourced.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The scope is interwar-style ultranationalism, and denial is not tied to the core doctrine; adherents vary.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Adherents are split; Fascist Italy did not criminalise it, but conservative strands would.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism subordinates all individuals and groups to the state, and ultranationalism rejects liberal democracy.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Strands differ: Maurras and kokutai backed established religion, Fascist Italy mostly did not; split.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Ultranationalism glorifies expansion and the supremacy of one nation, which implies empires governed for the ruling nation.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Rival nations' religious resistance is not a topic of the sources; inferred as rejected since it benefits other peoples.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The strands place national and state authority above religious-law legitimacy tests, though kokutai blended religion and state; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ultranationalism subordinates the individual to the nation-state and favours authoritarian leadership.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Class and identity divisions are subordinated to national unity, and class-based politics are rejected.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the interwar traditions emphasise hierarchy and traditional roles; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: The individual serves the nation, and traditionalist strands oppose it; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Fascist doctrine rejects both liberalism and socialism for a third way, calling left-right divisions obsolete.

alienated-labor.rationale: The strands reject class struggle and Marxism, so the alienation critique is not part of their frame; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Hostility to foreigners and minorities is a feature, though the Islam claim is anachronistic for the interwar scope; inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Strands differ: Maurras and kokutai held that authority comes from a divine or sacred order, while Mussolini placed it in the state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; strands differ on religion and state.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A strong, state-directed order is favoured over employer autonomy, but this specific issue is not addressed; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects laissez-faire and also rejects the liberal social-market compromise in favour of corporatist state control.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Militarism and national expansion are core ultranationalist features.

rich-first.rationale: Not stated; the nation is treated as an organic whole, which leaves regional inequality unaddressed.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Ultranationalism asserts the supremacy of one nation and pursues expansion, which rules out neutrality between blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from Japanese kokutai ultranationalism built on a hereditary imperial line; other strands, such as Fascist Italy, did not favour inheritance.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: the strands favour state-directed or syndicate-run finance rather than user-owned mutual banks.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from national supremacy and economic autarky, which reject foreign dictation of policy.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred: the strands subordinate individuals to the nation-state and do not rest on property-based franchise.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from hierarchy and militarist values; this egalitarian critique is foreign to the strands.

reification.rationale: Inferred from rejection of class-based socialism and Marxist analysis.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: No source addresses it; strands used state control of the press rather than a critique of wealth.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian leadership and rejection of liberal constitutionalism.

racial-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the supremacy of one nation over others and hostility to minorities; strands differ on race versus culture.

online-participation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of liberal democratic participation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian secrecy and state-first doctrine.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Strands differ: kokutai fused state and religion, while Fascist Italy and Maurras's circle made other accommodations.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Hostility to minorities is typical, but consumer boycotts are not a defining method; strands differ.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Authoritarian, leader-centred ultranationalism rejects liberal deliberative devices; inferred from its rejection of liberal democracy, no source addresses assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Strands differ, from state-Shinto kokutai doctrine to Maurras's Catholic traditionalism, and none addresses reinterpreting religious law; inferred as split.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sources do not address wealth concentration; strands differed, and the nation outranks class in all of them.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the martial, traditionalist values of interwar ultranationalist movements.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Japanese kokutai ideology tied the state to Shinto and other strands to national churches, so state atheism was opposed; inferred.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism glorifies the strong state's authority and force, so abolishing policing and imprisonment is rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Ultranationalism asserts the supremacy of one nation, so shared power with other communities is rejected; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates social provision to the State, so private charity is not preferred; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Authoritarian leadership is central, so term limits are disfavoured; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Doctrine rejects liberal democracy and the people's rule by numbers, so delegable voting is rejected; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; no stance can be inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Kokutai ideology and fascist doctrine kept public and religious authority male; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The Doctrine and kokutai ideology stress a patriarchal family; inferred.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Hostility to foreigners is typical of ultranationalism, so political rights for foreign residents are rejected; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: Housing policy is not addressed; strands differ on economics.

abolish-ip.rationale: Intellectual property is not addressed; strands differ on economics.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Interwar movements organised drilled youth organisations for national service; inferred from the militarist, state-first character.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The question is not addressed and strands split on the nuclear arsenal.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: National supremacy and sovereignty make foreign bases objectionable; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Ultranationalists glorify the nation's past and tend to deny its crimes; inferred.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Fascist corporatism claimed to organise production around labour for the nation; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects pacifism and holds war ennobles a people.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The mythic story of national decline and rebirth rests on an unbroken national essence.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Biological and traditional gender roles are stressed in these movements; inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The nation as a fixed unit with defined sex roles is typical; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism and kokutai ideology glorify sacrifice for the nation and state.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Fascism and kokutai thought cast politics as a mystical struggle for national rebirth; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Expansion and gathering of the nation's people under one state is typical of irredentism; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Strands split between cultural palingenesis and state primacy; the Doctrine of Fascism puts the state first.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Traditional hierarchy is the norm; inferred.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Supremacy of the nation and hostility to minorities mean national control of economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Merging peoples' lands into one national unit fits irredentism; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism puts the State above all groups and rejects class organisation, so unions independent of the state have no place.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Ultranationalism is described as hostile to class-based socialism, and the Doctrine denies class struggle as the basis of politics.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Sources do not address local services; regimes varied between state provision and private ownership.

second-chamber.rationale: The Doctrine rejects parliamentary democracy; a second chamber could be a corporative body, but this is inferred.

municipal-property.rationale: The Doctrine subordinates all economic activity to the State, leaving no place for community ownership independent of the nation-state.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Doctrine and integral nationalism insist on a single, strong, centralised State and organic national unity against divided authority.

family-wage.rationale: Ultranationalist regimes favoured the family and births for the nation, but no source addresses wages; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Ultranationalism has no position on drug approval; inferred indifference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ultranationalism has no position on ageing research; anachronistic, inferred indifference.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A state-primacy ideology would not accept money flows beyond state control; inferred from the Doctrine.

online-anonymity.rationale: Authoritarian ultranationalism demands state oversight of speech and association, so anonymity is disfavoured; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: The Doctrine holds that the individual exists only within the State, and the kokutai doctrine puts nation before self.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Doctrine calls fascism a spiritual conception of life and kokutai ideology rests on a sacred emperor, but strands differ on religion.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: These centralised states hold power in the national government, so regional powers would be revocable; inferred from the centralism of the sources.

gm-crops.rationale: Ultranationalism has no position on GM crops; inferred indifference.

dense-cities.rationale: Ultranationalism has no position on urban form; inferred indifference.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Ultranationalism asserts the interests of one nation or people over others; strands differ between race and nation and suppress sub-group organising.

racial-pride.rationale: Ultranationalism asserts national supremacy and often ties it to ancestry or blood; strands differ on race, so this is inferred.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects perpetual peace and sees expansion as vital, and Bugajski's account stresses militarism and expansion.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Irredentist and pan-nationalist strands claim all who share language and culture; inferred from the strand descriptions.

communal-electorates.rationale: Subordinates all groups to a single national state, so separate communal representation is rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Narratives of national decline typically blame hostile outsiders and internal enemies.

free-public-college.rationale: Sources are indifferent on tuition; strands varied.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not addressed; the strongly state-directed, growth and power-oriented approach disfavours price instruments.

future-generations.rationale: National continuity across generations is a theme of integral nationalism; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Militarist, hierarchical strands value martial virtues over a distinct feminine ethic; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Militarism and expansion are core features.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Authoritarian leaders favour freedom of action over public scrutiny; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: Autarkic, state-directed economies fit control of capital; inferred from Fascist corporatism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Interwar ultranationalists prized both the state's army and party militias, so adherents are split; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism holds that war ennobles a people and rejects pacifism, so refusing orders is condemned.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Class cooperation under the nation-state was preferred to independent union bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits are anachronistic and strands differ on welfare; no clear inference.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The nation-state's priority over individual and market constraints suggests resisting limits on state borrowing; inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Asserting one nation's supremacy sits badly with reordering world rules for others' benefit; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Ultranationalism exalts the nation-state and authoritarian leadership; it does not seek to smash the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Subordinating all activity to the nation-state leaves little room for diverse economic systems; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Ecosystem valuation was not addressed and strands differ on economics; no clear inference.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism treats the nation as a spiritual entity transcending individuals, and kokutai ideology does likewise.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt was not addressed and strands differ on welfare; no clear inference.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Integral nationalism stresses organic national unity and rejects grievance narratives within the nation; inferred.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Ultranationalism rejects universalist equality and sees nations as ranked, not grounded in a shared nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Authoritarian ultranationalism wants media aligned with the nation-state; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from strands tied to a national church or state cult, which claim their own religion as the nation's.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the organic nation and class solidarity that protect the rural base.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from militarism and national supremacy rejecting unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism and Maurras reject class struggle and socialism in favour of class unity under the nation.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; strands differ on custom versus modern law.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; strands split between traditional family roles and modern legal rights.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the single national language of the organic nation.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from state primacy over private action.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a unified nation-state, though some strands (kokutai) honour tradition.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from subordination of the individual to the nation-state.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from authoritarian state primacy and hostility to liberal legalism.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from assimilation demands on foreigners in integral nationalism.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the subordination of the individual to the nation-state and syndicalist organisation of labour under Fascist Italy; not stated directly.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the focus on national supremacy suggests suspicion of foreigners but no voting-procedure doctrine.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Strands differ, but most (integral nationalism, kokutai) tie the state to a national religion or tradition, so no equal recognition; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The sources describe ultranationalism as authoritarian and as rejecting liberal democracy and electoral competition as the test of legitimacy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Traditionalist and natalist doctrine of the nation suggests disapproval; no source states it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from authoritarian rule and the primacy of order; no source mentions internet access.

negative-income-tax.rationale: State direction of the economy in the national interest points away from a market-style cash transfer; inferred.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Doctrine of Fascism rejects universal suffrage in favour of rule by the state's elite, and women's public role was limited; inferred and varies by strand.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Strands differ on religion (Maurras valued Catholicism, fascists subordinated it); not addressed, so split.

race-social-construct.rationale: Many strands assert national or racial hierarchy as natural, though the Japanese and Italian forms stressed culture and spirit; inferred.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from traditional gender roles in the national family; strands did create women's organisations under the state, so the position is weak.

notes: The strands differ: Mussolini rejects race as the basis of the nation while Nazi and Ustase strands rest on it; Maurras is monarchist while fascists were not. Answers favour the shared core.
